summary.text: Leadership shifts into the strategic kingdom layer, where food, knowledge, troops, defenses, and public trust determine whether the realm can survive what is coming.

chapter.progressionIntent: Establishes the strategic loop and advances ordinary players through meaningful kingdom growth without side-quest gating.

summary.text: Stabilize the capital, establish a balanced first development plan, and prepare the realm for threats beyond the main gate.

text.text: Restore the Town Hall as a public command center.
Establish food, material, and storage continuity.
Begin one defensive or logistical research path.
Ready a trained garrison without emptying the civilian workforce.
Review the realm's readiness with its council.

choice.meaning: Choose people, knowledge, or defenses as the first visible priority; all required foundations still complete and no permanent build trap is created.

mainQuest.completionOutcome: The kingdom layer becomes a credible source of preparation, the realm avoids collapse, and the road beyond the walls reopens.

summary.text: Repair the food and storehouse chain before a ceremonial military parade consumes the realm's reserves.

mainStoryContribution.text: Connects abstract resource buildings to civilian survival and explains why later armies cannot exist outside the economy.

text.text: Audit the farm, road, and storehouse losses.
Choose a transparent ration plan with the local steward.
The kingdom tutorial highlights supply warnings earlier; no production rate or critical unlock changes.

summary.text: Investigate why recruits are leaving and resolve the conflict between training demands and families already stretched by the omen.

mainStoryContribution.text: Frames troops as people with obligations and introduces morale, support, and fair leadership before warzone armies appear.

text.text: Hear recruits, veterans, and families separately.
Correct one abusive or impossible training demand.
A veteran later explains why the garrison follows the champion through the main gate.
